title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Wednesday's AI-driven rally lifted the Nasdaq +1.6%, S&P 500 +1.3%, and Dow +0.5%, clawing back part of Tuesday's hot-CPI selloff; the dollar hit a fresh 19-month high on hawkish Fed rate-hike bets while bond markets were closed for Veterans Day.
Markets: Oil rose after two down sessions as the Trump administration signals a more restrained approach to Iran; gold slipped roughly 1% to just under $4,000.

Companies: CoreWeave (CRWV) jumped 25% after beating revenue estimates and raising 2026 sales guidance, lifting other AI/data-center and chip names and easing recent jitters over its rising borrowing costs.

Companies: Meta fell 2% after a WSJ report that United Airlines plans to block AI agents (e.g. Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots) from booking flights on its systems, highlighting friction between travel/retail firms and AI-agent commerce.
Companies: Applied Materials, Cisco, Cerebras, and Brookfield report earnings today after the close, with AMAT and Cisco seen as key AI-capex bellwethers.

Macro/Policy: WSJ's lead story warns the global economy looks vulnerable to an AI investment bust - a slowdown would hit exports in weaker economies and squeeze retail investors worldwide who piled into tech stocks; governments have limited fiscal room to respond.
Macro/Policy: Today's data slate includes weekly jobless claims, existing home sales, and the monthly Treasury budget.
